title: Guide for Downloading Large Datasets to a Supercomputer Using SRA Toolkit
author: Jacob Heldenbrand
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kb6csre
materials: The SRA Toolkit is a complex piece of software that can be difficult to navigate, as the documentation is extensive and error messages are not always able to provide clarity when failures occur. In an effort to maximize the Toolkit’s utility, we have devised a protocol for downloading thousands of SRA files and converting them into FASTQ files in a reasonable amount of time. To make the process as simple as possible, our protocol anticipates and adjusts for likely errors. While this guide has a limited lifespan in the face of regular updates to the Toolkit, we hope that our instructions will be of help to the community, as they summarize a lot of disjoint information already floating around on the Web.

The download procedure is normally a two-step process: first grab the SRA files from the repository, then convert SRA files to FASTQ on the cluster. A few preparatory steps will help avoid bottlenecks. vdb-config Run the following command to execute vdb-config (located within the SRA toolkit bin folder). This may require X11 forwarding (ssh –X flag on login to cluster). ./vdb-config –i ./vdb-config –i This opens a GUI where the location of the dbGaP project space can be configured. Set this to Project_Space. If downloading dbGaP data, specify the repository key location. Make sure this is done before downloading the refseq data below, as the tool will not allow you to point to a directory in which the sra and refseq subdirectories are not empty. refseq download To convert an SRA file to the FASTQ format, fastq-dump must normally download reference data stored in a refseq database at NCBI. However, this creates a bottleneck when trying to scale up conversions of many files, as the reference data end up being downloaded repeatedly for every file batch. To circumvent this bottleneck, we manually downloaded all the reference files located at https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sra/refseq/ . While this is a large download of ~40GB, it only needs to be done once. Furthermore, the SRA Toolkit is configured to download any missing reference files if it cannot find them later during the SRA to FASTQ conversion stage. Thus, if new reference files are added to the repository between your bulk reference download and the actual data conversion, you should still get correct results when running fastq-dump. To download the reference files, copy the contents of https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sra/refseq/ into an Excel sheet, grab the names of each file, and put them in a file named /base/refseq_download/list_all_refseqs.txt. Use the following bash script as a wrapper to call the python script that downloads the reference files. Wrap the bash script in a qsub and submit it to a compute node. Using ten download processes in parallel by breaking up /base/refseq_download/list_all_refseqs.txt into 10 batches will increase efficiency. /base/refseq_download/download_parallel_wrapper.sh #!/bin/bash python base/refseq_download/download_refseqs_parallel.py 0 & python base/refseq_download/download_refseqs_parallel.py 1 & python base/refseq_download/download_refseqs_parallel.py 2 & python base/refseq_download/download_refseqs_parallel.py 3 & python base/refseq_download/download_refseqs_parallel.py 4 & python base/refseq_download/download_refseqs_parallel.py 5 & python base/refseq_download/download_refseqs_parallel.py 6 & python base/refseq_download/download_refseqs_parallel.py 7 & python base/refseq_download/download_refseqs_parallel.py 8 & python base/refseq_download/download_refseqs_parallel.py 9 & wait /base/refseq_download/download_parallel_wrapper.sh #!/bin/bash python base/refseq_download/download_refseqs_parallel.py 0 & python base/refseq_download/download_refseqs_parallel.py 1 & python base/refseq_download/download_refseqs_parallel.py 2 & python base/refseq_download/download_refseqs_parallel.py 3 & python base/refseq_download/download_refseqs_parallel.py 4 & python base/refseq_download/download_refseqs_parallel.py 5 & python base/refseq_download/download_refseqs_parallel.py 6 & python base/refseq_download/download_refseqs_parallel.py 7 & python base/refseq_download/download_refseqs_parallel.py 8 & python base/refseq_download/download_refseqs_parallel.py 9 & wait /base/refseq_download/download_refseqs_parallel.py import sys import subprocess N = int(sys.argv[1]) filenames = [] with open('/base/refseq_download/list_all_refseqs.txt') as F: for line in F: name = line.strip() filenames.append(name) # Start at position N and go to the end in 10 step intervals for i in filenames[N::10]: subprocess.check_call("~/.aspera/connect/bin/ascp \ -i ~/.aspera/connect/etc/asperaweb_id_dsa.openssh -k 1 -T -l800m \ anonftp@ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov:/sra/refseq/{0} \ /base/Project_Space/refseq/".format(i), shell=True) /base/refseq_download/download_refseqs_parallel.py import sys import subprocess N = int(sys.argv[1]) filenames = [] with open('/base/refseq_download/list_all_refseqs.txt') as F: for line in F: name = line.strip() filenames.append(name) # Start at position N and go to the end in 10 step intervals for i in filenames[N::10]: subprocess.check_call("~/.aspera/connect/bin/ascp \ -i ~/.aspera/connect/etc/asperaweb_id_dsa.openssh -k 1 -T -l800m \ anonftp@ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov:/sra/refseq/{0} \ /base/Project_Space/refseq/".format(i), shell=True)

steps.title: Create SRA Batch List
steps.instruction: Create a text file containing the list of SRA IDs to be downloaded for each batch in the specified directory.

substeps.instruction: Create a text file at /base/batches/batch_lists/batchX.txt (where batchX is the current batch name).
List the SRA IDs (e.g., SRR123, SRR234) within the file.

steps.title: Generate Prefetch Scripts and JobList
steps.instruction: Use the generateBatchScripts.prefetch.py script to automatically create individual bash scripts for each SRA ID and a master JobList.txt for the Anisimov Launcher.

substeps.instruction: Run the script using the command: python generateBatchScripts.prefetch.py /base/batches/batch_lists/batchX.txt batchX
Verify that bash scripts are generated in /base/batches/batchX/[SRA_ID]/[SRA_ID].sh
Verify that the JobList.txt is created in /base/jobLists/batchX_JobList.txt

steps.title: Create and Submit Prefetch qsub Script
steps.instruction: Construct and submit a qsub script to schedule the prefetch jobs via the Anisimov Launcher.

substeps.instruction: Create a qsub script in /base/qsubs/batchX_prefetch.qsub.
Configure resources: for a batch of 1,200 samples, use 80 nodes with 32 ppn (e.g., #PBS -l nodes=80:ppn=32) and a walltime of 1:15:00.
Set aprun flags: -n 1280, -N 16, -ss, and -d 2 (assuming 15 samples per node).
Ensure the -noexit flag is used in the aprun command to prevent a single failure from killing the entire job.
Direct output to /base/qsubs/logs/batchX_prefetch.log.

steps.title: Monitor and Clean Up Downloads
steps.instruction: Monitor the download progress and remove temporary files to prevent subsequent download failures.

substeps.instruction: Monitor the /base/Project_Space/sra folder using 'ls -l /base/Project_Space/sra | head'.
If the folder size does not grow for approximately five minutes, kill the job using 'qdel JobID'.
Navigate to /base/Project_Space/sra and delete temporary/lock files using: rm *.tmp.aspera-ckpt, rm *.tmp.partial, rm *.lock, rm *.tmp, rm *.vdbcache.cache, and rm *.vdbcache.

steps.title: Verify SRA Downloads and Iterate
steps.instruction: Identify missing SRA IDs and repeat the download process until all IDs are accounted for.

substeps.instruction: Run the verification script: python /base/scripts/checkSRAsDownloaded.py /base/batches/batch_lists/batchX.txt
Copy any missing SRA IDs into a new batch file (e.g., batchX.1, batchX.2) in /base/batches/batch_lists/.
Repeat the prefetch steps, reducing requested resources in the qsub script for each subsequent iteration.

steps.title: Generate Fastq-dump Scripts and JobList
steps.instruction: Generate the scripts required to validate SRA files and convert them to FASTQ format.

substeps.instruction: Run the script: python /base/scripts/generateBatchScripts.fastq-dump.py ../batches/batch_lists/batchX.txt batchX
This script creates validation and conversion bash scripts and updates the JobList.txt in /base/jobLists/.

steps.title: Create and Submit Fastq-dump qsub Script
steps.instruction: Construct and submit a qsub script to execute the validation and conversion process.

substeps.instruction: Create a qsub script in /base/qsubs/batchX_fastq-dump.qsub.
Configure resources: for 1,200 samples, use 80 nodes with 32 ppn and a walltime of 6:00:00.
Set aprun flags: -n 1280, -N 16, -ss, and -d 2.
Direct output to /base/qsubs/logs/batchX_fastq-dump.log.

steps.title: Verify FASTQ Conversion
steps.instruction: Verify that all expected FASTQ files were successfully created.

substeps.instruction: Run the verification script: python /base/scripts/checkFastqsConverted.py /base/batches/batch_lists/batchX.txt /base/fastq_files/batchX
If any files are missing, inspect the validation_error files in /base/Project_Space/validation_failures/ and re-download the SRA files if necessary.
